title: How to Stop Hair Loss from Zepbound: Prevention and Treatment
summary: Discover how to stop hair loss from Zepbound with proven strategies. Learn why tirzepatide causes hair shedding, evidence-based prevention methods, treatment options, and realistic recovery timelines from this temporary side effect.
body_text: Hair loss is a concerning side effect reported by some patients taking Zepbound (tirzepatide) for weight management. This FDA-approved medication works by reducing appetite and promoting significant weight reduction, but rapid metabolic changes can trigger temporary hair shedding known as telogen effluvium. Understanding why this occurs and implementing targeted nutritional strategies can help prevent or minimize hair loss during treatment. This guide provides evidence-based approaches to protect hair health while benefiting from Zepbound therapy, including prevention strategies, treatment options, and realistic recovery timelines for patients experiencing medication-related hair thinning. Quick Answer: Hair loss from Zepbound is typically prevented and treated through adequate protein intake, nutritional supplementation, gradual weight loss, and addressing deficiencies in iron, zinc, and vitamins. Zepbound-related hair loss is usually telogen effluvium triggered by rapid weight loss rather than direct drug effects on hair follicles Prevention requires 0.8-1.2 grams protein per kilogram daily plus adequate iron, zinc, biotin, and vitamins A, C, D, and E Treatment includes correcting nutritional deficiencies, topical minoxidil, and moderating weight loss to 1-2 pounds weekly Hair typically recovers within 6-12 months after stabilizing weight loss and normalizing nutrition Dermatology referral is indicated for severe, progressive, or patchy hair loss suggesting alternative diagnoses We offer compounded medications and Zepbound®. Compounded medications are prepared by licensed pharmacies and are not FDA-approved. References to Wegovy®, Ozempic®, Rybelsus®, Mounjaro®, or Saxenda®, or other GLP-1 brands, are informational only. Compounded and FDA-approved medications are not interchangeable. Table of Contents Why Zepbound May Cause Hair Loss How to Prevent Hair Loss While Taking Zepbound Treatment Options for Zepbound-Related Hair Loss Long-Term Hair Recovery After Zepbound Use Scientific References Frequently Asked Questions LOSE WEIGHT WITH MEDICAL SUPPORT — BUILT FOR MEN Your personalised programme is built around medical care, not willpower. No generic diets. No guesswork. Just science-backed results and expert support. Find out if you’re eligible Take the quiz Learn more Why Zepbound May Cause Hair Loss Zepbound (tirzepatide) is a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 ( GLP-1 ) receptor agonist approved by the FDA for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight with weight-related comorbidities. [1] [2] Alopecia (hair loss) is reported in the clinical trials for Zepbound and is listed in the FDA-approved prescribing information as an adverse reaction. [1] [2] The most likely mechanism linking Zepbound to hair loss is telogen effluvium , a temporary condition triggered by physiological stress. Rapid weight loss—a primary effect of tirzepatide therapy—can shift hair follicles prematurely from the active growth phase (anagen) into the resting phase (telogen). Approximately two to four months after this metabolic stress, affected hairs are shed simultaneously, resulting in noticeable thinning. Rapid weight loss is a well-established trigger for telogen effluvium according to the American Academy of Dermatology. Additional contributing factors may include nutritional deficiencies that develop during rapid weight reduction. Patients taking Zepbound often experience reduced caloric intake due to decreased appetite and delayed gastric emptying. Without adequate dietary planning, deficiencies in protein, iron, zinc, biotin, and essential vitamins can compromise hair follicle health. Gastrointestinal side effects such as nausea (reported in 24-30% of patients), vomiting (8-21%), and diarrhea (18-24%) may further impair nutrient intake and absorption. [1] It is important to note that there is no established direct pharmacological mechanism by which tirzepatide itself damages hair follicles. The association appears indirect, mediated primarily through the metabolic and nutritional consequences of significant weight loss rather than through receptor-mediated effects on hair growth cycles. Telogen effluvium differs from other types of hair loss such as androgenetic alopecia (pattern baldness) or alopecia areata (patchy hair loss with potential autoimmune origins). Strategy Specific Action Target / Dose Evidence Level / Notes Adequate protein intake Consume lean poultry, fish, eggs, legumes, low-fat dairy 0.8–1.2 g per kg body weight daily Supports keratin synthesis; Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics guidance Key micronutrient repletion Correct iron, zinc, biotin, vitamins A, C, D, E deficiencies Iron 8–18 mg; zinc 8–11 mg; biotin 30 mcg daily Lab testing (ferritin, CBC, TSH, vitamin D) recommended before supplementing Moderate weight loss rate Discuss dose titration with provider to slow weight reduction 1–2 lbs per week; ~5–10% over 6 months Reduces metabolic stress on follicles; CDC recommendation Topical minoxidil Apply 2% or 5% solution/foam to affected scalp areas Once daily (foam) or twice daily (solution) FDA-approved for pattern loss; off-label for telogen effluvium; initial shedding possible Iron supplementation Supplement if ferritin below 30–50 ng/mL, under medical supervision 65–200 mg elemental iron daily Iron deficiency without anemia is a common telogen effluvium contributor Low-level laser therapy (LLLT) Use FDA-cleared LLLT device consistently on affected scalp Per device instructions Moderate evidence; off-label for telogen effluvium; adjunctive use only Dermatology referral Refer if hair loss is severe, progressive, patchy, or persists beyond 6 months Evaluate for alopecia areata or androgenetic alopecia Telogen effluvium is non-scarring; full recovery typical with appropriate management How to Prevent Hair Loss While Taking Zepbound Preventing hair loss during Zepbound therapy requires a proactive, multifaceted approach focused on optimizing nutrition and moderating the rate of weight loss. While specific guidance for GLP-1/GIP therapy is evolving, principles adapted from weight management research can help maintain hair health. Nutritional strategies form the cornerstone of prevention. Patients should aim for adequate daily protein intake, generally 0.8-1.2 grams per kilogram of body weight according to the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics. High-quality protein sources include lean poultry, fish, eggs, legumes, and low-fat dairy products. Adequate protein provides the amino acids necessary for keratin synthesis, the structural protein comprising hair shafts. Additionally, ensuring sufficient intake of iron (18 mg daily for premenopausal women, 8 mg for men and postmenopausal women), zinc (8-11 mg daily, with attention to copper balance), biotin (30 mcg daily), and vitamins A, C, D, and E supports follicular health. Excessive supplementation should be avoided, as high doses of fat-soluble vitamins (A, E) can be toxic. Patients should consider working with a registered dietitian experienced in weight management to develop an individualized meal plan that meets nutritional requirements despite reduced appetite. A daily multivitamin supplement may be appropriate, though supplementation should not replace whole food sources. Baseline laboratory assessment—including complete blood count, ferritin, TSH, and vitamin D—can identify pre-existing deficiencies requiring targeted repletion. Moderating weight loss velocity is equally important. While Zepbound is highly effective for weight reduction, aiming for a gradual loss of 1-2 pounds per week (approximately 5-10% over 6 months) as recommended by the CDC may reduce metabolic stress on hair follicles. Patients should discuss realistic weight loss goals with their healthcare provider and consider dose titration strategies that balance efficacy with tolerability. Maintaining adequate hydration and managing gastrointestinal side effects through dietary modifications or antiemetic therapy can also improve overall nutritional status during treatment. Treatment Options for Zepbound-Related Hair Loss When hair loss occurs despite preventive measures, several treatment options can support hair regrowth and minimize further shedding. The management approach should be individualized based on the severity of hair loss, underlying nutritional status, and patient preferences. Nutritional repletion remains the primary intervention. If laboratory testing reveals specific deficiencies, targeted supplementation is indicated. Iron deficiency, even without anemia, commonly contributes to telogen effluvium; ferritin levels below 30-50 ng/mL may warrant iron supplementation (typically 65-200 mg elemental iron daily) under medical supervision. Vitamin D insufficiency (25-hydroxyvitamin D below 20-30 ng/mL, per Endocrine Society guidelines) should be corrected with appropriate supplementation. Biotin supplementation is generally not recommended unless a true deficiency is suspected or confirmed, as deficiency is rare in the US. Patients should be advised that biotin can interfere with certain laboratory assays, including troponin and thyroid function tests, and should be discontinued at least 72 hours before blood testing. Topical minoxidil (2% or 5% solution or foam) is FDA-approved for pattern hair loss and may be used off-label for telogen effluvium by potentially prolonging the anagen phase and stimulating follicular activity. Application once (foam) or twice (solution) daily to the affected scalp areas is standard, though patients should be counseled that an initial increase in shedding may occur during the first 2–4 weeks as miniaturized hairs are replaced by healthier growth. Minoxidil is generally well-tolerated, with local irritation being the most common side effect. Low-level laser therapy (LLLT) devices are FDA-cleared for promoting hair growth in androgenetic alopecia and may provide adjunctive benefit through photobiomodulation of follicular cells, though use for telogen effluvium is off-label. While evidence quality is moderate, some patients experience improved hair density with consistent use. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injections represent an emerging option, though evidence supporting efficacy specifically for medication-related telogen effluvium remains limited, and treatment is typically not covered by insurance. Patients should be referred to a dermatologist if hair loss is severe, progressive despite intervention, or accompanied by scalp inflammation, scarring, or patchy distribution suggesting alternative diagnoses such as alopecia areata or androgenetic alopecia. Long-Term Hair Recovery After Zepbound Use The prognosis for hair recovery following Zepbound-related telogen effluvium is generally favorable, as this condition is typically self-limited once the triggering stressor is addressed. Understanding the expected timeline and factors influencing recovery helps set realistic patient expectations and guides ongoing management decisions. Natural recovery timeline : Telogen effluvium characteristically resolves spontaneously once metabolic stress subsides and nutritional status normalizes. After the triggering event (rapid weight loss), affected follicles remain in telogen for approximately three months before shedding. New anagen hairs then begin growing, but visible regrowth typically requires an additional 3–6 months to become cosmetically apparent. Therefore, patients may not observe significant improvement until 6–12 months after implementing preventive strategies or slowing weight loss. During this period, continued shedding may occur as the follicular cycle normalizes, which can be distressing but does not indicate treatment failure. Factors influencing recovery include the duration and severity of nutritional deficiency, the rate of weight loss stabilization, and individual genetic factors affecting hair growth rates. Patients who achieve weight stability, maintain adequate protein and micronutrient intake, and address underlying deficiencies typically experience complete or near-complete hair density restoration. However, individuals with pre-existing androgenetic alopecia (pattern hair loss) may notice that baseline thinning becomes more apparent during the telogen effluvium episode and may not fully reverse without specific treatment for that condition. Ongoing monitoring should include periodic assessment of nutritional markers, particularly in patients continuing Zepbound therapy for weight maintenance. If hair loss persists beyond 6 months despite appropriate interventions, or if new patterns of hair loss develop, further dermatological evaluation is warranted to exclude alternative diagnoses. Abnormal laboratory values should be rechecked after 2-3 months of treatment. Patients should be reassured that telogen effluvium is non-scarring and does not cause permanent follicular damage, and with appropriate management, hair density typically returns to pre-treatment levels. Maintaining realistic weight loss goals, prioritizing nutritional adequacy, and practicing patience during the recovery period are essential components of successful long-term outcomes. Scientific References ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) injection, for subcutaneous use . FDA Approves New Medication for Chronic Weight Management . Frequently Asked Questions Is hair loss from Zepbound permanent? No, Zepbound-related hair loss is typically temporary telogen effluvium that resolves once weight stabilizes and nutrition normalizes. Most patients experience complete or near-complete hair density restoration within 6-12 months with appropriate nutritional management. How much protein should I eat to prevent hair loss on Zepbound? Aim for 0.8-1.2 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight daily from sources like lean poultry, fish, eggs, and legumes. Working with a registered dietitian can help ensure adequate intake despite reduced appetite from tirzepatide therapy. Should I stop taking Zepbound if I experience hair loss? Do not discontinue Zepbound without consulting your healthcare provider. Hair loss can often be managed through nutritional optimization, moderating weight loss rate, and treating deficiencies while continuing therapy for its intended metabolic benefits. title: Voice AI Is the Interface. Process Design Is the Innovation.
summary: The latest news, product updates, and industry insights from Marr Labs on AI in mortgage lending and servicing.
body_text: Voice AI is having a moment. ‍ The Information recently spotlighted a wave of startups building AI-powered voice agents across industries, from restaurants to fintech to mortgage lending. It’s exciting coverage for a technology that’s quietly matured over the past 12 to 18 months. But amid all the excitement, something more fundamental is happening: the real innovation isn’t just in the voice. It’s in the workflow. The ability to speak naturally with AI is no longer the hard part . Advances from OpenAI, Deepgram, Google, and others have made real-time, human-like voice interaction finally possible and affordable. What separates a flashy demo from a real business solution isn’t better speech quality. It’s better process design. ‍ At Marr Labs, we’ve seen this firsthand. We build voice agents for mortgage lenders that don’t just “talk.” They work. Our agents qualify borrowers, capture key data, and route the call while staying compliant and integrated with client CRMs and telephony systems. The value isn’t in the voice alone. It’s in the orchestration: who gets called, when, under what conditions, what’s said, what’s captured, and what happens next. ‍ In other words, the agent is just the interface. The magic is in what it connects to and how it fits into the business process. That’s where many new entrants get it wrong. It’s tempting to focus on the model, the voice, the latency numbers. And yes, those matter. But when voice AI gets deployed in the real world — in mortgage, healthcare, logistics, or hospitality — it meets a wall of operational complexity: Compliance requirements Human handoff scenarios CRM and LOS integrations Timing sensitivities Multi-party workflows Solving for those is where the true differentiation lies. We’ve learned, for example, that a one-second delay in warm-transferring a borrower can mean a lost lead. That the wrong phrasing during a qualification call can trigger regulatory issues. That transferring too early or too late undermines trust. Designing for these details and iterating them over time is what makes a voice agent effective. The market is starting to see that. The Information noted that companies like Marr Labs are already running real-time qualification calls on behalf of lenders, not as a proof of concept, but as a core operational tool. And that’s just the beginning. The winners in this space won’t be the ones with the smoothest-sounding bots. They’ll be the ones that make voice AI invisible, woven into the flow of business, supporting people and processes without getting in the way. Voice AI isn’t a product. It’s infrastructure. And the best infrastructure disappears. ‍

title: Mozambique LNG: Clarification by TotalEnergies
summary: Paris, November 20, 2025 – Following the recent filing of a complaint before the French National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor’s Office (Pnat) in Paris against persons unknown and against TotalEnergies for “complicity in war crimes, torture and enforced disappearances” in Mozambique between July and September 2021, the Company – which has not been formally served with this […]
body_text: Paris, November 20, 2025 – Following the recent filing of a complaint before the French National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office (Pnat) in Paris against persons unknown and against TotalEnergies for “complicity in war crimes, torture and enforced disappearances” in Mozambique between July and September 2021, the Company – which has not been formally served with this complaint by the plaintiff – firmly rejects all such accusations. This complaint follows a September 2024 article published by the digital media outlet Politico . In the context of the deadly terrorist attacks of March 2021 claimed by Islamic State-affiliated jihadist group (Al-Shabab), the Politico article alleged that Mozambican soldiers committed serious abuses near the Mozambique LNG site between June and September 2021. However, during this period, Mozambique LNG personnel were not present on site given that it had been evacuated in early April 2021. Following the attack on Palma in March 2021, which had tragic consequences for the local population, Mozambique LNG evacuated all staff from the site. The Mozambican army subsequently took control of the Afungi site, the airport, and the port, with the aim of restoring security in the area. It is within this context of counter-terrorism efforts that the Politico allegations were reported. It should additionally be noted that well before the Mozambique LNG project began the Cabo Delgado province was already facing violent attacks from Islamist groups. In light of the seriousness of these accusations, TotalEnergies wishes to share the following information transparently with all stakeholders: TotalEnergies strongly and categorically rejects Politico 's allegation that Mozambique LNG or the Company had, or could have had, any knowledge of the acts of violence reported in the Politico article and underpinning the complaint. All internal verifications conducted with our stakeholders confirm that neither Mozambique LNG nor, a fortiori, TotalEnergies had received at the time any information suggesting that such acts had been committed. Since the first article published on this matter in September 2024, TotalEnergies has requested that Politico provide access to any data, supporting evidence or documentation that would substantiate the events reported. In response, Politico has repeatedly refused to provide any such data. For several months now, TotalEnergies has maintained contact with Politico and responded fully and transparently to its numerous inquiries. However, in light of the deliberately selective use of these detailed responses in Politico 's reporting, in the interests of transparency TotalEnergies published the entirety of its exchanges with Politico . TotalEnergies' stakeholders may therefore visit the dedicated webpage on its website, where all communications published by TotalEnergies and Mozambique LNG since the first Politico article in September 2024 can be found. Stakeholders will be able to see for themselves Politico 's questions and accusatory editorial stance as well as its selective cherry picking of the Company's responses. TotalEnergies regrets that some media outlets and associations persist with efforts to infringe upon the Company's reputation by attempting to place responsibility on Mozambique LNG and TotalEnergies for the severe consequences resulting from the March 2021 terrorist attack of Palma and, more recently, for the acts of extreme violence that Politico alleges were perpetrated by the Mozambican army during summer 2021. On the relationship between Mozambique LNG and the Joint Task Force (JTF) Security in Mozambique, as in all sovereign states, is the responsibility of the national authorities. In Mozambique as in all other nations, it is the state's security forces that ensure the protection of the site. In this context, the relationship between Mozambican security forces and the Afungi gas projects, including Mozambique LNG, was governed by a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between the State of Mozambique and the project. This MoU, now expired, was intended to support the logistical needs of a joint military-police unit (JTF) tasked with protecting the site, and imposed strict human rights commitments notably including the training of more than 5,000 personnel in the Voluntary Principles on Security and Human Rights (VPSHR), a grievance mechanism, and procedures for removal in the event of misconduct. Incidents reported through this grievance mechanism, as well as through other established grievance reporting channels, were documented and reported by Mozambique LNG in a transparent manner. The complaints and grievances received by Mozambique LNG did not substantiate any of the allegations made by Politico and which were set out in the complaint announced in the press. On the investigations requested by Mozambique LNG and TotalEnergies In November 2024, in respect of the sovereignty of Mozambique and its national laws, Mozambique LNG formally requested the Mozambican authorities to open an official investigation into these allegations in order to determine the facts. In March 2025, TotalEnergies welcomed the announcement by the Attorney General of Mozambique confirming that a criminal investigation had been launched into these allegations. Mozambique LNG is fully cooperating with the authorities in this framework. TotalEnergies has also requested that the Mozambique National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) conduct its own independent investigation into these allegations. The Company has committed to publishing the NCDH's report. On the humanitarian situation and human rights In December 2022, TotalEnergies mandated Jean-Christophe Rufin to carry out an independent assessment of the humanitarian situation in the Cabo Delgado province. His report , along with the action plan subsequently adopted by Mozambique LNG, was made public in May 2023 and helped strengthen numerous local development programs and support mechanisms for host communities. This initiative reflects the Company's commitment to human rights and to the long-term development of local communities. About Mozambique LNG Mozambique LNG is a liquefied natural gas project being developed in Cabo Delgado, northern Mozambique. TotalEnergies (26.5%) is a partner in the project alongside other international companies and Mozambique's national oil company. TotalEnergies believes that the socio-economic development of Cabo Delgado – which Mozambique LNG aims to support – is in the best interest of Mozambique and its people, particularly those located in the vulnerable northern province of the country. The Company remains committed to supporting the development of the project, led by Mozambique LNG, while ensuring the safety of the personnel working at the Afungi site and the respect of local communities' rights. ***

body_text: Inhibikase Therapeutics Announces Third Quarter 2025 Financial Results and Highlights Recent Activity November 14, 2025 4:01pm EST Download as PDF Related Documents 10-Q Filing PDF HTML XBRL ZIP HTML BOSTON and ATLANTA, Nov. 14, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Inhibikase Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: IKT) (“Inhibikase” or “Company”), a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company developing therapeutics to modify the course of cardiopulmonary diseases namely, Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (“PAH”), today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 and highlighted recent developments. “During our third quarter of 2025, we continued to position the Company to advance IKT-001 toward a late-stage clinical trial in PAH,” said Mark Iwicki, Chief Executive Officer of Inhibikase. “We expect to initiate our Phase 2b clinical study of IKT-001, our prodrug of imatinib mesylate, in PAH during the fourth quarter of 2025.” Recent Developments: Advancement of IKT-001 as a therapy in PAH: The proposed Phase 2b IMPROVE-PAH trial is a multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of approximately 150 PAH participants. Participants under IMPROVE-PAH will be randomized 1:1:1 to receive 300 mg IKT-001, 500 mg IKT-001, or placebo once daily for 26 weeks, in addition to stable background PAH therapy. The Company’s bioequivalence studies previously confirmed that 500 mg of IKT-001 has comparable exposure in humans to 383 mg of imatinib. The primary efficacy endpoint is change in pulmonary vascular resistance at Week 26. Secondary endpoints include 6-minute walk distance, World Health Organization functional class, and pharmacokinetics. The study protocol also includes an interim safety review for study continuance by the Data Safety Monitoring Board with at least 50 patients at 12-weeks of follow-up. The Company has been actively working with potential sites and presently expects to initiate IMPROVE-PAH in the fourth quarter of 2025. Appointed veteran biopharma executive Timothy Pigot as the Company’s Chief Commercial and Strategy Officer. The Company also expects to present at the Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference in London on Monday, November 17th, 2025. Financial Results Cash Position: As of September 30, 2025, cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $77.3 million as compared to $97.5 million as of December 31, 2024. Net Loss: Net loss for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, was $11.9 million, or $0.13 per share, compared to a net loss of $5.8 million, or $0.65 per share in the quarter ended September 30, 2024. Net loss for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, was $35.5 million, or $0.40 per share, compared to a net loss of $15.4 million, or $2.03 per share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2024. R&D Expenses: Research and development expenses were $7.6 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, compared to $4.2 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2024. Research and development expenses were $23.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, which includes a non-cash write-off of in-process research and development of $7.4 million and $1.8 million of stock-based compensation expense, both associated with the Company’s acquisition of CorHepta in February 2025, compared to $10.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2024. SG&A Expenses: Selling, general and administrative expenses for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 were $5.6 million, compared to $1.6 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2024. Selling, general and administrative expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 were $16.8 million, which includes $1.0 million of severance expenses resulting from the transition of senior executives in the Company during the year, compared to $5.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2024. About Inhibikase (www.inhibikase.com) Inhibikase Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: IKT) is a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company developing therapeutics to modify the course of cardiopulmonary diseases namely, PAH, that arise from aberrant signaling through the Abelson Tyrosine Kinase, and type III receptor tyrosine kinases including platelet derived growth factor receptors and c-KIT. Our lead product candidate is IKT-001, a prodrug of imatinib mesylate, for PAH which is an orphan indication. PAH is a progressive, life-threatening disease characterized by pulmonary vascular remodeling and elevated pulmonary vascular resistance that affects approximately 50,000 Americans.
